course_name_original: Experimentación en Química y Tecnología Química
course_name_en: Experimentation in Chemistry and Chemical Technology
prerequisites: Prior knowledge of Mathematics, Chemistry and Thermodynamics is advisable.

It is recommended to have passed or be enrolled in: Fundamentos de los Procesos Químicos, Cinética y Reactores Químicos, Operaciones Básicas I, Operaciones Básicas II, Control e Instrumentación de Procesos Químicos y Termodinámica Química Aplicada a la Ingeniería.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge about material and energy balances, biotechnology, mass transfer, separation operations, chemical reaction engineering, reactor design, and valorization and transformation of raw materials and energy resources.

Ability for the design and management of applied experimentation procedures, especially for the determination of thermodynamic and transport properties, and modeling of phenomena and systems in the field of chemical engineering, systems with fluid flow, heat transfer, mass transfer operations, chemical reaction kinetics and reactors.
Ability to design, manage and operate simulation, control and instrumentation procedures for chemical processes.
Measure transport properties (viscosity, thermal conductivity and diffusion coefficients).
Operate fluid flow systems applicable in Chemical Engineering.
Operate different types of heat exchangers applicable in Chemical Engineering.
Understand the operation and mode of operation of distillation columns.
Operate different types of ideal reactors.

syllabus_topics: Practice 1. Determination of liquid viscosities.
Introduction to viscosity measurement.
Application to identify the behavior of Newtonian and non-Newtonian fluids.
Determination of the variation of a Newtonian fluid's viscosity with temperature.
Practice 2. Experimental determination of molecular diffusion coefficients in liquid phase.
Introduction to the basic concept of molecular diffusion, foundation of component separation performed in basic mass transfer operations.
Application to the measurement of an electrolyte diffusion coefficient by conductivity measurements.
Practice 3. Experimental determination of liquid-liquid equilibrium data for a ternary system.
Introduction to the fundamentals of liquid-liquid equilibrium and the handling of triangular diagrams, basic aspects of solvent extraction.
Determination of the binodal curve and the tie line of a ternary system.
Practice 4. Experimental determination of liquid-vapor equilibrium data for a binary system.
Introduction to the fundamentals of liquid-vapor equilibrium, a basic aspect for distillation and rectification operations.
Determination of steady-state compositions by pycnometry.
Practice 5. Heat exchangers.
Compare the behavior of coil and plate heat exchangers.
Experimental determination of individual and global heat transfer coefficients.
Practice 6. Experimental determination of wet-bulb temperature.
Introduction to the basic concepts of psychrometry, foundation of humidification operations.
Practice 7. Distillation in a packed column.
Familiarize the student with distillation operations, studying the rectification of a binary mixture in a packed column.
Determine the mass transfer efficiency for a distillation operation in a packed column.
Practice 8. Filter press
Familiarization with the operation of a pilot-scale filtration equipment, operating in two ways: at constant speed and constant pressure.
Propose a model for cake filtration and experimentally determine its parameters.
Practice 9. Kinetic study in a batch reactor.
Familiarize the student with the planning and execution of experiments to study the reaction rate in a laboratory batch reactor.
Determine the influence of concentration and temperature for a catalyzed homogeneous liquid-phase reaction, propose a kinetic model and calculate its kinetic parameters.
Practice 10. Continuous stirred tank reactor.
Familiarize with the operation of a stirred tank reactor and the most important operating variables in steady and unsteady state.
Study the influence of stirring speed on the degree of mixing through residence time distribution.
Perform kinetic analysis in a continuous stirred tank reactor, determining the overall reaction order, kinetic constant, and activation energy.
Practice 11. Solving material and energy balances with a process simulator: HYSYS.
Introduce the student to solving material and energy balances in reaction processes and/or separation processes using a commercial chemical process simulation program (HYSYS).
Gain experience in using a computer process simulation program, an essential tool in engineering, understanding the inherent difficulties and its potential.
Practice 12. Gas absorption in a packed column.
Estimation of entrainment and flooding flow rates in a packed column.
Verification of mass conservation equations in an absorption column.

assessment_methods.method: Written exam with questions and problems
Continuous evaluation sheet (attitude and aptitude in laboratory work)

assessment_rules: To pass the subject, a minimum of 4.0 must be obtained in the written exam and in the practice report. All practicals must be completed, and attendance to introductory expository classes is required. A final weighted score of at least 5.0 is needed to pass. If minimum grades are not met in any individual practice report, the final grade for the report section will be the lowest score obtained for the unpassed aspect, and the subject will not be passed. In the extraordinary call, students with approved reports and continuous evaluation only need to take a written exam. Students who failed the practice report and/or continuous evaluation must take a practical exam and a written exam.
